bio.jane/contract.noScientificClaim: Stores the user's choice of enzymes; computes nothing.
bio.jane/contract.question: Save these enzymes as a named collection.

description: Save a set of enzymes as a named collection in your Enzyme Collections panel, so a scan that found the enzymes worth keeping ends by keeping them instead of asking you to retype the list. Every name is checked against the cut catalog first and an unknown one refuses the whole save by name, because a collection that silently lost two enzymes is worse than one that was never made. An existing collection is never overwritten unless you say so.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

activate.description: make it the active collection, which is what the panel does when you create one — every enzyme parameter that is left unset then scopes to it.

enzymes.description: the enzyme names to save — wire these from a scan (enzyme_cut_counts, digest_fragments) or from enzyme_collection rather than typing them, so the set is one the engine has already resolved.

name.description: what to call the collection, as it will read in the panel.

replace.description: overwrite a collection that already has this name. Left false, a name clash refuses and says which collection it would have replaced.

name: save_enzyme_collection

active.description: whether this collection is now the one an unset enzyme parameter resolves to

collection.description: the name it was saved under

created.description: true for a new collection, false when an existing one of the same name was replaced

enzymes.description: the names as saved, de-duplicated in the order given — wireable straight into a scan
